sample_unit: LLM-generated patient leaflets (plus one clinician-written comparator leaflet)

links.outcome: Readability of LLM-generated DMEK leaflets (FKG, FRE, ARI, Gunning Fog) versus clinician leaflet
links.effect: Readability varied across LLMs; Claude 3.7 Sonnet had strong readability and the top LLM score (77.8%), while the clinician leaflet scored highest overall (92%). Individual readability grade values are not reported in the abstract.
links.quote: Claude 3.7 Sonnet had the top LLM score (77.8%), with strong readability and referencing.

links.outcome: Misinformation detection in LLM-generated patient leaflets
links.effect: ChatGPT-4 and Microsoft CoPilot scored lowest due to limited reliability and misinformation; none of the LLMs matched clinician leaflet quality (92%).
links.quote: ChatGPT-4 and Microsoft CoPilot scored the lowest due to limited reliability and misinformation.

links.outcome: Presence and quality of references in LLM-generated leaflets
links.effect: Claude 3.7 Sonnet had strong referencing, while ChatGPT-4o (70.9%) lacked references.
links.quote: ChatGPT-4o followed closely (70.9%) but lacked references.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the readability, accuracy, and reliability of patient education leaflets generated by various LLMs compared to a clinician-written leaflet, but does not test a specific deployment practice or safeguard intervention.
